people.label: Robert "Bob" Lazar
people.sub: Los Alamos contract technician, 1982; claimant from 1989 of work on alien propulsion at a facility he calls S-4 near Papoose Lake; convicted Nevada felon, 1990
people.narrative: Bob Lazar is the origin point of the best-known claim in the field and, on the opened record, he is a contract electronics technician rather than the physicist the claim requires. In 1982 he worked at Los Alamos, and the Los Alamos Monitor of 27 June 1982 described him on its front page as 'a physicist at the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility'. That description is the strongest documentary thread in his favour and it carries its own qualification: the Los Alamos telephone directory page that also lists his name states on its face that it covers Department of Energy employees and the outside contractor Kirk-Mayer, and a Los Alamos colleague interviewed on tape in 1996 said Lazar 'was a contractor' under Kirk Mayer. In 1989 he told KLAS-TV in Las Vegas, first silhouetted under the pseudonym 'Dennis' and then under his own name, that between December 1988 and April 1989 he had worked at a facility called S-4, about fifteen miles south of Groom Lake, back-engineering the propulsion of nine disc-shaped craft fuelled by a stable isotope of element 115. In 1991 he fixed that account in datable form by narrating it himself on a forty-minute videotape produced with his friend Gene Huff. The credential half of his account has been checked by named people and does not survive: no institutional record of the MIT or Caltech degrees exists, and the professor he named as a Caltech instructor turned out to teach at Pierce Junior College, where Lazar had taken at least one of his classes. The credential question is Tier 1 rather than gossip because Lazar's own reported education, listing a 1978 Pacifica University BS alongside the MIT and Caltech degrees, is printed in his Pre-Sentence Report of 27 July 1990, a Clark County court document produced after he pleaded guilty to felony pandering. What makes him a node is proximity to the claim, not credibility: no clearance is documented anywhere in the opened record, no office, and no physical trace of anything he describes.
people.tierRationale: Node tier C: proximity to the programme, not credibility, on the same discipline the board applies to mark-mccandlish. Custody proximity 0 because no opened record places him in contact with any material; access 0 because his claimed S-4 access is a claim and not documented access, and the board does not score A on a claim; disclosure role 3 because his entire documented function since 1989 has been publication of a claim, and the 1989 broadcasts are the single event that put Area 51 into worldwide public consciousness. Status 'alive' with no date: no death record exists and no birth record was opened, so the node carries no birth year and no age.

conflicts: His own 1991 narration says 'for the duration of my employment at S4 I was paid by the United States Navy'. The W-2 form as others describe it names a 'Department of Naval Intelligence', which is not an entity that exists; the Office of Naval Intelligence sits inside the Department of the Navy. The two statements are not the same statement, and the board carries the discrepancy rather than resolving it, because the form itself was not opened.

The Teller anecdote has a date problem. His 1991 narration puts the Los Alamos Monitor jet-car story and Edward Teller's Los Alamos speech on the same day. Tom Mahood's 2018 retrospective puts the Monitor article on 27 June 1982 and Teller's lecture on the following day. The newspaper's own date is fixed, so both cannot be right. The anecdote survives as 'within a day' and is carried as such.

The sentence is described differently by two reliable routes. The Las Vegas Review-Journal of 21 August 1990 reports probation with 150 hours of community service and psychotherapy. Douglas Dean Johnson, working from the court file, describes a three-year suspended sentence with probation, completed. These are compatible readings of one disposition but they are not the same wording, and no session has reconciled them against the judgment of conviction itself.

people.label: John Olsen Lear
people.sub: Son of the Learjet founder and a documented pilot; from a dated statement of 29 December 1987 one of the field's most prolific claimants; present at two of the three 1989 desert viewings with Lazar
people.narrative: John Lear is the rare figure in this cluster whose ordinary career is fully documented and whose extraordinary claims are not. He was born on 3 December 1942, the son of William Powell Lear, founder of Lear Jet, and Moya Olsen Lear, and his papers sit inside the William P. and Moya Olsen Lear Family Collection at The Museum of Flight Archives. In May 1966 he was one of the pilots on a Learjet 24 flight around the world that set a large number of international records. His place in this cluster is chronological as much as evidentiary: his own public claim document is dated 29 December 1987, roughly eighteen months before Lazar reached KLAS-TV, and it circulated through the ParaNet bulletin board in early 1988, setting the frame that Lazar's 1989 account then fitted into. He and Lazar had met by 1988, and he was present at the first and third of the three Wednesday-night desert viewings in the spring of 1989, on 22 March and 5 April, the second of which ended with the group detained by the Lincoln County Sheriff. He is carried here as an early promoter and a viewing participant, not as an eyewitness to any facility. He died on 29 March 2022.
people.tierRationale: Node tier C: proximity to the claim rather than to any programme. Custody proximity 0 and access 0 because nothing in the opened record gives him a clearance, an office or contact with material; his aviation career is documented and is not programme access. Disclosure role 2 because his 29 December 1987 statement is a dated, preserved artefact that shaped the field's frame before Lazar entered it, which is a real publication role short of the 3 carried by the originating claimant.

people.narrative: Gene Huff has two distinct roles in this cluster and the board should carry both, because the second is the structural one. He is a Las Vegas real-estate appraiser who met Lazar in 1985 and was socialising with him by 1988, and he is the named witness to the three Wednesday-night desert viewings of March and April 1989, the third of which ended with the group detained by the Lincoln County Sheriff. His first-hand claim is about lights seen from Tikaboo Valley and nothing more: he does not claim to have been inside any facility. His second role is that he wrote and co-produced the 1991 videotape, The Lazar Tape and Excerpts from the Government Bible, which is the artefact in which Lazar's whole account is fixed in datable form and which is the strongest opened source in this cluster. That makes him the publisher of the cluster's primary document, and the board treats publication as a structural fact. He is also the source of the $958.11 figure that circulates as the amount on Lazar's W-2: it is his recollection, in his own 1995 synopsis, of a cheque he says he saw.
people.tierRationale: Node tier C: proximity to the claim, not credibility. Custody proximity 0 and access 0 because he has never claimed to have been inside anything or to have handled any material, and no record gives him any clearance. Disclosure role 2 because he authored and produced the videotape that carries the account, which is a genuine publication role but downstream of the claimant himself.

people.label: Tom Mahood
people.sub: Retired civil and traffic engineer with an MS in physics; author of the otherhand.org Lazar investigation, the most detailed documentary examination of the account in existence
people.narrative: Tom Mahood is the custody and analysis point for most of the documentary record in this cluster, and without a node for him the board's case-against edges have nothing to originate from. He describes himself on his own site as a former civil engineer and traffic engineer for Orange County, California, with a Master's degree in physics from Cal State Fullerton. His otherhand.org investigation reprints the Los Alamos Monitor front page of 27 June 1982, both Las Vegas Review-Journal reports of 1990, Mark Farmer's 1996 taped interview with an anonymised Los Alamos colleague, and David L. Morgan's physics critique, and it quotes Lazar's 1990 Pre-Sentence Report. His conclusion on the credentials is flat: 'Lazar never attended either CalTech or MIT. Of this I am certain of beyond a reasonable doubt.' His 2018 retrospective is the single best case-against document in the cluster precisely because it concedes what is true, granting that Lazar is 'amazingly believable', that Mahood himself initially found the story plausible, and that Lazar showed genuine technical cleverness. His counter-explanation is that there is nothing at Papoose Lake, that S-4 is a designator attaching to a Tonopah Test Range radar facility, and that the account began as a cover story after security caught Lazar bringing friends to watch classified tests in April 1989.
people.tierRationale: Node tier C: he is adjacent to the claim as an investigator, with no programme proximity of any kind. Custody proximity 0 and access 0. Disclosure role 2 because he forced a documentary record into the open and hosts the only openable copies of several primary items, which is the same function the board already credits to the-black-vault and john-greenewald, one step below the originating claimant.

entities.label: Element 115: the Lazar claim and moscovium
entities.sub: The claimed stable, machinable superheavy fuel of the S-4 propulsion account, set beside the real element 115 synthesised in 2003, assigned in 2015 and named moscovium in 2016
entities.desc: THIS NODE RECORDS A CLAIM AND A SEPARATE PHYSICAL FACT THAT HAPPEN TO SHARE A NUMBER, AND IT IS NOT AN ASSERTION THAT THEY ARE THE SAME THING. The claim is Lazar's: that a stable isotope of element 115 was the fuel of the reactor he says he worked on, that it could be machined into triangular wedges and stored, that 223 grams would run for twenty to thirty years, and that its nuclear binding field, which he calls gravity A and identifies with the strong nuclear force, extends past the perimeter of the atom so that it can be accessed and amplified. The fact is that element 115 was synthesised in a Dubna and Lawrence Livermore experiment published in Physical Review C on 2 February 2004, that the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry assigned discovery priority on 30 December 2015, and that the name moscovium was approved on 28 November 2016. The two do not meet. Lazar's claim is not that element 115 exists, which was never controversial and was predicted popular physics from 1969; it is that a stable isotope of it exists and that he handled half a pound of it. Nothing in the 2004 paper, the 2015 priority decision or the 2016 naming touches that. Equally, the hostile version, that he invented a number and got lucky, is also wrong: the island of stability near element 114 was in Scientific American in April 1969 and in undergraduate textbooks by 1970. The correct finding is neither prescient nor fabricated from nothing. It is available prior art, used. The board carries the claim as a claim and the element as an element, on one node so that the collision is visible in one place.

claims.text: WHAT WAS ACTUALLY SYNTHESISED. Element 115 was first reported in Oganessian et al., 'Experiments on the synthesis of element 115 in the reaction 243Am(48Ca,xn)291-x115', Physical Review C volume 69, article 021601(R), published 2 February 2004, a Dubna and Lawrence Livermore collaboration. The abstract reads: 'With a beam dose of 4.3x10^18 248-MeV Ca48 projectiles, we observed three similar decay chains consisting of five consecutive alpha decays, all detected in time intervals of about 20s and terminated at a later time by a spontaneous fission with a high-energy release (total kinetic energy ~220MeV). At a higher bombarding energy of 253MeV, with an equal Ca48 beam dose, we registered a different decay chain of four consecutive alpha decays detected in a time interval of about 0.5s, also terminated by spontaneous fission.' The isotopes are 288 and 287, at cross sections of roughly 3 picobarn and 1 picobarn.

claims.text: A PRECISION POINT USUALLY GOT WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry assigned discovery priority for element 115 on 30 December 2015 to 'the Dubna-Livermore-Oak Ridge collaborations', and the basis given is work 'starting in 2010, and subsequently confirmed in 2012 and 2013, have met the criteria for discovery'. The priority statement therefore rests on the 2010 to 2013 work and not on the 2003 experiment. The Joint Working Party report is Karol, Barber, Sherrill, Vardaci and Yamazaki, Pure and Applied Chemistry 88 (2016) 155.

claims.text: THE COLLISION, STATED WITHOUT OVERSTATEMENT AND WITHOUT SOFTENING. entities.label: Los Alamos Monitor, 27 June 1982, 'LA Man Joins The Jet Set - At 200 Miles An Hour'
entities.sub: Terry England's front-page story on Lazar's jet-powered Honda, which describes him in the newspaper's own voice as a physicist at the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility
entities.desc: This is the strongest documentary thread in Bob Lazar's favour and the node must carry its qualification in the same breath, or it will misrepresent the record in the direction the credulous literature already pulls. The artefact is real: a front-page story with a byline, a date and page numbers, in a daily newspaper published in Los Alamos on Sunday 27 June 1982, about a jet-powered Honda Lazar had built, which describes him in the paper's own voice as 'a physicist at the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility'. It was printed seven years before the UFO claim and cannot have been manufactured for it. What it is not is an employment record. The description is what Lazar told the reporter, and two independent strands of the opened record place him as a contract electronics technician instead: the Los Alamos telephone directory page that also lists his name states on its face that it covers Department of Energy employees and the outside contractor Kirk-Mayer, and an anonymised Los Alamos colleague interviewed on tape in 1996 said that Lazar 'was a contractor' under Kirk Mayer. The article also matters as a date peg for the Edward Teller anecdote, and there it creates a problem rather than solving one, because Lazar's own 1991 narration places the newspaper story and Teller's Los Alamos speech on the same day while the article's date is fixed at 27 June and Teller's lecture falls on the following day.
entities.tierRationale: Node tier B: a dated, openable contemporary primary publication seven years ahead of the claim, which is the same footing the board gives other contemporaneous press artefacts. C0 and A0 as a document. D1 because its disclosure role is incidental rather than intended: it is a story about a car that only became evidentiary later.

entities.label: Clark County, Nevada felony pandering file, 1990 and 1996
entities.sub: The 1990 complaint and police affidavit, the 27 July 1990 Pre-Sentence Report listing Pacifica, MIT and Caltech, the 20 August 1990 sentence, and the 1996 refusal of the petition to withdraw the plea
entities.desc: THE COURT RECORD IS THE SPINE OF THE LAZAR QUESTION AND IT SHOWS TWO SEPARATE THINGS, THE SECOND MORE USEFUL THAN THE FIRST. The first is a conviction: Lazar was arrested on 5 June 1990, pleaded guilty to felony pandering on 18 June 1990, and was sentenced on 20 August 1990 by District Judge Jack Lehman to probation with 150 hours of community service, an order to stay away from brothels and a year of psychotherapy, the judge remarking that he 'could not make a determination regarding his claims'. In 1996 Lazar petitioned to withdraw the plea, the District Attorney opposed on the ground that his new claims were irrelevant to admitted and documented criminal activity, and the court refused, so the conviction stands. The second thing the file shows is what makes the credential question Tier 1 rather than gossip. Lazar's Pre-Sentence Report of 27 July 1990 records his own reported education: a 1978 Bachelor of Science in Physics and Electronic Technology from Pacifica University, a 1982 Master of Science in Physics from MIT, and a 1985 Master of Science in Electronic Technology from Caltech. That is not a television claim that can be blamed on a paraphrasing journalist. It is what he told a court under sentence, in writing, through a probation officer. Every institutional check since has failed to confirm any of the three. Gene Huff's rebuttal of 15 May 1995, that the probation officer misunderstood a pair of correspondence courses, is carried beside it and is not adopted.
entities.tierRationale: Node tier C: a court file about the claimant, adjacent to the programme rather than inside it. C0 and A0 as a document. D1 because its effect on the public record is real but incidental to its purpose. Its claims are Tier 1 for what the documents themselves show, which is what court records are always Tier 1 for on this board, and nothing here is Tier 1 for the truth of anything Lazar told the court.

timeline.text: District Judge Jack Lehman sentenced Lazar to probation rather than prison, with 150 hours of community service, an order to 'stay away from brothels and undergo psychotherapy', and a year of psychotherapy, saying he 'could not make a determination regarding his claims'. The same report describes Lazar's claim as of that date as being that 'the U.S. government was testing alien spacecraft at the Nevada Test Site, 65 miles northwest of Las Vegas', which is a different named place from the one the claim later settled on.
timeline.source: Las Vegas Review-Journal, 21 August 1990, p 2C, by Warren Bates, https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/lv-review-journal-8-21-1990/

timeline.label: The Lazar Tape fixes the whole claim in datable form
timeline.text: Tri-Dot Productions publishes 'The Lazar Tape and Excerpts from the Government Bible', forty minutes, created by Gene Huff and Bob Lazar. It is the strongest artefact in the cluster and the one opened by this board: its English auto-generated captions, 1,046 segments to 38:39, were read in full on 18 September 2026. Every element-115 claim, every S-4 description and the Teller anecdote carry timestamps in it.
timeline.source: Internet Archive item 'antigravity', https://archive.org/details/antigravity ; captions via YouTube video kc10m6HFbDE

timeline.label: Petition to withdraw the 1990 guilty plea is refused
timeline.text: Lazar petitioned to withdraw the plea, citing post-traumatic stress, hidden federal records and inadequate legal representation. The District Attorney opposed, arguing 'that Lazar's new claims were irrelevant to his admitted and documented criminal activity'. The judge denied the petition and the conviction stands.
timeline.source: Douglas Dean Johnson, 31 January 2021, https://douglasjohnson.ghost.io/bob-lazar-and-his-nevada-felony-conviction/

timeline.label: Physicist David L. Morgan publishes the physics critique
timeline.text: Dr David L. Morgan, a particle physicist, publishes 'A Physicist's Critique', revised April 2001. Three objections: that the strong nuclear force 'has NOTHING TO DO WITH GRAVITY'; that the nuclear force 'extends out to about the same distance away from a nucleus NO MATTER HOW MASSIVE THE NUCLEUS IS'; and, crucially without needing any model of gravity, that if the antimatter must be made on board then 'your system produces NO NET ENERGY AT ALL!!'
timeline.source: Dr David L. Morgan, 'A Physicist's Critique', https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/a-physicists-critique/

timeline.label: Stanton Friedman publishes 'The Bob Lazar Fraud'
timeline.text: Friedman, a nuclear physicist who spent his career arguing that UFOs are real craft, publishes the credential investigation, updated January 2011. He located the professor Lazar named as a Caltech instructor: 'I located Dr. Duxler. He's a Pierce Junior College physics prof, and never taught at Caltech.' He records the directory page's own scope statement and describes the W-2 as totalling 'under $1000.00'. The heaviest denial in the cluster comes from a proponent, not a debunker.
timeline.source: Stanton T. Friedman, 'The Bob Lazar Fraud', https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/the-bob-lazar-fraud-2/

timeline.label: Element 115 synthesis published in Physical Review C
timeline.text: Oganessian et al., 'Experiments on the synthesis of element 115 in the reaction 243Am(48Ca,xn)291-x115', Physical Review C 69, 021601(R), a Dubna and Lawrence Livermore collaboration. The isotopes are 287 and 288, at cross sections of roughly 1 and 3 picobarn, observed as chains of consecutive alpha decays running to completion within about twenty seconds and about half a second. Nothing about them is stable, machinable or storable.
timeline.source: Physical Review C 69, 021601(R), https://journals.aps.org/prc/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevC.69.021601

timeline.label: CPSC: United Nuclear, the company, fined $7,500 after pleading guilty to three counts
timeline.text: CORRECTS THE STANDARD FRAMING. It is widely repeated that 'in 2006, Lazar pleaded guilty' to a Federal Hazardous Substances Act violation. The CPSC's own release of 20 July 2007 says the COMPANY pled guilty, to three criminal counts, before U.S. Chief Magistrate Lorenzo F. Garcia: 'United Nuclear Scientific Supplies LLC, of Edgewood, N.M., founded and operated by Robert Lazar, was fined $7,500 and received three years probation.' Robert Lazar and accountant Joy White appear in the separate civil consent decree.
timeline.source: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, Release 07-249, https://www.cpsc.gov/Newsroom/News-Releases/2007/New-Mexico-Company-Fined-Ordered-To-Stop-Selling-Illegal-Fireworks-Components

timeline.label: The CIA's U-2 and OXCART history, declassified, acknowledges Groom Lake
timeline.text: The National Security Archive posts Electronic Briefing Book 443, edited by Jeffrey T. Richelson, on the CIA history 'The Central Intelligence Agency and Overhead Reconnaissance: The U-2 and OXCART Programs, 1954-1974' by Gregory Pedlow and Donald E. Welzenbach, declassified that summer. This is the documented half of the hub's geography and it is a statement about Groom Lake, NOT about Papoose Lake.
timeline.source: National Security Archive EBB 443, https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/node/3324

timeline.label: IUPAC assigns discovery priority for element 115
timeline.text: Priority went to 'the Dubna-Livermore-Oak Ridge collaborations', on the basis of work 'starting in 2010, and subsequently confirmed in 2012 and 2013'. A precision point usually got wrong in both directions: the priority statement rests on the 2010 to 2013 work, not on the 2003 experiment. The Joint Working Party report is Karol, Barber, Sherrill, Vardaci and Yamazaki, Pure and Applied Chemistry 88 (2016) 155.
timeline.source: IUPAC, 30 December 2015, https://iupac.org/discovery-and-assignment-of-elements-with-atomic-numbers-113-115-117-and-118/

timeline.label: Element 115 formally named moscovium
timeline.text: The name moscovium, symbol Mc, was formally approved on 28 November 2016 and announced on 30 November 2016, proposed by the discoverers at Dubna, Oak Ridge, Vanderbilt and Lawrence Livermore, in recognition of the Moscow region. This event is regularly presented as vindicating the Lazar claim. It does not: his claim requires a STABLE isotope that can be machined and stored, and no such isotope exists.
timeline.source: IUPAC, 30 November 2016, https://iupac.org/iupac-announces-the-names-of-the-elements-113-115-117-and-118/

timeline.label: FBI searches United Nuclear Scientific in a Michigan homicide investigation
timeline.text: A two-page Laingsburg, Michigan police report records an 'Agency Assist' supporting an FBI search of United Nuclear Scientific in aid of 'a homicide investigation out of Houghton, MI involving poison', and records that Lazar consented to the search. The underlying case is the thallium death of Janel Sturzl, 31, on 22 December 2015. Lazar is not recorded as a suspect. The report was obtained by Tim McMillan under a local open-records request.
timeline.source: Laingsburg Police Department report, published by The Black Vault, https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/documents-on-2017-bob-lazar-united-nuclear-raid-laingsburg-police-department/

timeline.label: Bob Lazar: Area 51 and Flying Saucers released digitally in the United States
timeline.text: Jeremy Corbell's 97-minute documentary, narrated by Mickey Rourke, featuring Lazar, George Knapp and Joy White. Letterboxd lists United States digital release on 1 November 2018, United Kingdom physical on 4 December 2018 and United States physical on 8 December 2018. The widely cited '4 December 2018' is the UK physical date; IMDb returned HTTP 403 and no distributor record was opened.
timeline.source: Letterboxd record, https://letterboxd.com/film/bob-lazar-area-51-and-flying-saucers/

timeline.label: Mahood's retrospective: nothing at Papoose Lake, S-4 is a Tonopah radar facility
timeline.text: Tom Mahood publishes his mature assessment: there is 'nothing at Papoose Lake', S-4 refers to a radar facility at the Tonopah Test Range, and the alien-craft narrative began as a cover story after the April 1989 detention. It concedes in the same document that Lazar is 'amazingly believable' and that Mahood initially found the story plausible. T.D. Barnes reaches the same radar-site conclusion by an unrelated route in 2026.
timeline.source: Tom Mahood, https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/looking-at-the-bob-lazar-story-from-the-perspective-of-2018/

timeline.label: Papoose Lake photographed from the air on a legal overflight: nothing there
timeline.text: Tyler Rogoway of The War Zone publishes aerial images taken on a pilot's authorised flight directly over Papoose Lake: 'nothing appears to be there, just as satellite images show. There isn't even an access road and, as you can see, the lakebed is flooded, which is a fairly common occurrence.'
timeline.source: Tyler Rogoway, The War Zone, https://www.twz.com/32951/pilots-rare-trip-around-area-51-includes-pics-of-range-targets-drone-bases-ufo-legends

timeline.label: John Lear dies
timeline.text: The Museum of Flight Archives authority record states: 'John Lear died on March 29, 2022.' He was born 3 December 1942, the son of William Powell Lear and Moya Olsen Lear, and his materials sit within the William P. and Moya Olsen Lear Family Collection.
timeline.source: The Museum of Flight Archives, https://archives.museumofflight.org/agents/people/4962

gaps.text: The half-lives of the moscovium isotopes are NOT ASSERTED. The primary 2004 Physical Review C paper gives decay-chain durations, not isotope half-lives. What the paper itself supports, and all that the board claims, is that the isotopes are short-lived alpha emitters produced one atom at a time at picobarn cross sections.

There is no physical trace of the claim: no sample of any material, no photograph of any craft, no document bearing an 'S-4' designator, no manifest, no badge, and no personnel record of any kind. After thirty-seven years this cluster rests on one man's testimony, one friend's corroboration of lights in the desert, one videotape, one newspaper article about a jet-powered Honda, and a court file. The board should carry that plainly and the hub's high edge degree should never be mistaken for it.
